question: What gestational age range defines a term pregnancy for normal labour?
explanation: Normal labour typically occurs at term, which is clinically defined as a gestation lasting from 37 weeks up to the end of 42 weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: Which of the following represents the passenger in the context of labour dynamics?
explanation: The passenger refers to the fetus, whose size, presentation, and position greatly influence the mechanism of labour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h1)

question: What term is used to describe the positional adjustments a fetus makes while navigating the pelvis?
explanation: The series of physical adaptations the fetus makes through the birth canal are collectively called the cardinal movements. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: Why does the fetus perform multiple positional changes during its transit through the pelvis?

options.A: To stimulate increased frequency of uterine contractions
options.B: To conserve fetal oxygen reserves during the second stage
options.C: To adapt its head diameters to the changing pelvic dimensions
options.D: To accelerate the detachment of the placenta from the wall

explanation: The bony pelvis changes shape from the inlet to the outlet, requiring the fetal head to rotate and flex to fit through the tightest spaces. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h2)

question: What anatomical landmark of the maternal pelvis signifies that engagement has occurred when reached by the biparietal diameter?
explanation: Engagement is confirmed when the widest part of the fetal head descends to the level of the ischial spines, corresponding to station zero. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: When does engagement typically take place in a first-time mother (primigravida)?

options.A: A few weeks before the onset of labour
options.B: Immediately following the rupture of membranes
options.C: Only after the second stage of labour begins
options.D: During the third stage alongside the placenta

explanation: First-time mothers often experience head engagement late in the third trimester, weeks before actual labour contractions commence. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h3)

question: Which smaller fetal head diameter is achieved when optimal flexion occurs?
explanation: Flexion tucks the chin to the chest, replacing the wider occipitofrontal diameter with the compact suboccipito-bregmatic diameter. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: What anatomical structure of the pelvis is primarily responsible for triggering internal rotation of the fetal head?
explanation: The sloping pelvic floor muscles act like a slide, directing the leading occiput to rotate forward toward the pubic symphysis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h4)

question: Which maternal bone acts as a pivoting fulcrum during the extension of the fetal head?
explanation: The occiput pivots around the lower border of the pubic symphysis, allowing the face and chin to sweep upward and out. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: What part of the fetus emerges first during the extension phase of a normal vertex delivery?
explanation: As the head extends around the pubic bone, the vertex, brow, face, and chin successively sweep over the perineum and emerge. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of restitution immediately following the birth of the head?

options.A: An intentional manual maneuver performed by the attending midwife
options.B: The sudden relaxation of the maternal perineal floor muscles
options.C: The untwisting of the neck vessels and tissues after internal rotation
options.D: The immediate contraction of the fetal shoulder girdle muscles

explanation: Restitution is a passive unwinding movement caused by the relief of torsion placed on the neck tissues during internal rotation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)

question: Which part of the fetal body is delivered immediately after the anterior shoulder during the expulsion phase?
explanation: The anterior shoulder delivers first under the pubic arch, after which the trunk flexes laterally to allow the posterior shoulder to sweep over the perineum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T005#GNS226_U3_T005_h6)
